No discrete introduced correctness or security defect was established. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `281e565f9a6a24cda18ecd3097400ee17d5c4214` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A focused owner-level repair with meaningful subprocess evidence and no identified code defect, pending upgrade validation. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (linked_artifact): Recorded Testbox evidence exercises the production stdio/client path with real ENOENT and official-launcher EACCES failures, observes retained failures without another spawn, and verifies native configuration reads without Node on PATH. EBADARCH is injected; macOS upgrade continuity remains a separate compatibility gap. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (linked_artifact): Recorded Testbox evidence exercises the production stdio/client path with real ENOENT and official-launcher EACCES failures, observes retained failures without another spawn, and verifies native configuration reads without Node on PATH. EBADARCH is injected; macOS upgrade continuity remains a separate compatibility gap. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 10 items | Introduced scope and merge ownership: Reviewed the pinned merge-base-to-head production, test, and documentation hunks. The test merge has the recorded base and exact PR head as its ordered parents; package-only catalog selection survives that merge.
Current main still needs the fix: The fetched main transport lacks retained spawn failures and still limits interpreter-based launcher execution to Bun; its catalog currency lacks terminal-failure cancellation.
Shipped selection contract: The latest supplied release, v2026.9.5, supports desktop-first and package-first candidate lists containing desktop executables. The introduced package-only branch removes those candidates specifically for managed passive catalogs. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Codex session catalog discovers native conversations through a managed app-server process. Its launch and refresh owners turn configured session homes into searchable catalog entries and report failures to operators. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Configured session homes] --> B[Catalog owner] B --> C[Installed Codex launcher] C --> D[Native app server] D --> E[Session catalog entries] C --> F{Permanent launch failure} F --> G[Retain failure and stop retries] G --> H[Operator advisory and Doctor] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Existing macOS catalogs that used a working desktop executable can become unavailable when their installed Codex package cannot run. Published v2026.9.5-to-candidate upgrade evidence covering catalog availability and successful update completion remains missing. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Record the published v2026.9.5 updater-to-candidate macOS transition, showing catalog availability and successful update completion when the optional Codex executable cannot run. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.

Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Root-cause cluster Relationship: `fixed_by_candidate` Canonical: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154313 Summary: This PR is a candidate repair for the reported executable-refusal loop; earlier capture-retention fixes address adjacent failures. Members: - `canonical`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154313 - The report identifies the macOS Intel spawn refusal and persistent resident-catalog retries addressed here. - `adjacent_distinct`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153038 - Merged work bounds capture retention and closed-client retries, without providing this terminal executable-failure handling. - `adjacent_distinct`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153468 - Merged work owns crash reclamation and legacy capture diagnostics, which this branch reuses. Proposal only: this assessment does not dispatch repair, suppress jobs, mutate sibling items, close, or merge anything. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Verify the published upgrade transition (recommended)** Record the published updater completing the candidate transition with existing macOS catalog state, including the optional executable-failure case. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep launch-failure handling with the existing transport and catalog owners, with demonstrated upgrade continuity for package-only macOS catalogs. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes for the launch-failure mechanism: a missing executable exercises the real startup boundary, supported by the recorded subprocess regressions. The reporter's exact Intel executable remains unidentified, and this review did not execute a current-main reproduction. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes for retaining terminal failures and stopping catalog scheduling through existing owners; the intentional executable-selection change still needs upgrade validation. The introduced package-only branch removes those candidates specifically for managed passive catalogs. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/managed-binary.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ec9c1a13db8938e5a3eaa51fca2e981cde2395a9/extensions/codex/src/app-server/managed-binary.ts), [ec9c1a13db89](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ec9c1a13db8938e5a3eaa51fca2e981cde2395a9)) - **Dependency contract applies:** The transport directly invokes the official Codex JavaScript launcher with the Gateway interpreter, and the new failure observer interprets that launcher's native-child error output. This establishes the dependency-specific inspection requirement. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-stdio.ts:45`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/281e565f9a6a24cda18ecd3097400ee17d5c4214/extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-stdio.ts#L45), [281e565f9a6a](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/281e565f9a6a24cda18ecd3097400ee17d5c4214)) - **Official launcher inspected directly:** Verified dependency ownership through the backing repository's origin URL and personally read the sibling launcher at the recorded revision. It selects platform packages from process architecture, prints native spawn errors and exits with status 1, and forwards termination signals. This is the available sibling revision, not the different revision cited in the PR body. ([`codex-cli/bin/codex.js`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340/codex-cli/bin/codex.js), [6b9826e3aa83](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/6b9826e3aa83b1a5947db50f4332cb9c65f1b340)) - **Recorded behavior proof:** The complete supplied PR body records Testbox runs covering real ENOENT subprocess startup, official-launcher native EACCES, retained failure without a second spawn, and native configuration reads without Node on child PATH. These results were supplied evidence, not executions performed during this review.
